source.label: Wikipedia: the set was “begun around 1757 and not finished until 1765”
Wikipedia: “a series of paintings depicting various animals and plants”

highlight.text: The composition [is] skilful, the colouring of the [hydrangea] harmonious, and the feathers of the fowls [lifelike]. The elegance of the whole picture makes [it] truly decorative.

source.author: Nippon Bukkyō Shinbi Kyōkai
source.title: Shinbi taikan: Selected Relics of Japanese Art, vol. XIII

source.label: Morrison: “Especially he favoured cocks and hens as a subject”
Wikipedia: the Colorful Realm is “a set of thirty hanging scrolls”

work.text: A very common theme among his work is birds, in particular hens and roosters, though several of his more famous paintings depict cranes, cockatoos, parrots, and phoenixes.

moment.text: [Kōrin’s] taste rather turned to [flowers] and herbage for subject while [Jakuchū] took animals: and while they are not alike in the use of the brush, in colour scheme, or in their tastes, yet they are a pair of master-hands in the school of decorative painters.

source.author: Nippon Bukkyō Shinbi Kyōkai
source.title: Shinbi taikan: Selected Relics of Japanese Art, vol. XIII

matters.text: He held strong ties to Zen Buddhist ideals, and was considered a lay brother (koji); but he was also keenly aware of his role within a Kyoto society that was becoming increasingly commercial.
